subject: Astronomy & Space
title: JUICE: Jupiter's Icy Moons Explorer
description: A quick win: understand JUICE: Jupiter's Icy Moons Explorer.

hook.text: ESA's JUICE mission launched in 2023 to study Jupiter's three icy moons: Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto.

buildup.text: After arriving in 2031, it will perform multiple flybys of all three moons before entering orbit around Ganymede.

discovery.text: It will be the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's—a milestone in planetary exploration.

twist.text: JUICE will probe Ganymede's magnetic field, subsurface ocean, and ice shell—searching for conditions that could support life.

climax.text: Combined with Europa Clipper, JUICE will give us the most complete picture ever of Jupiter's ocean worlds.

punchline.text: Three icy moons, one orbiter. The first mission to orbit another world's moon.

quiz.question: What milestone will JUICE achieve at Ganymede?
options: It will be the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's Moon
It will be the first mission to land on an icy moon's surface
It will be the first spacecraft to enter Jupiter's atmosphere

details.summary: ESA's JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer), launched in April 2023, will study Jupiter's three largest icy moons: Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto. details.whyItMatters: JUICE complements Europa Clipper by focusing on Ganymede — the solar system's largest moon. Together, these missions will characterize three potential ocean worlds around a single planet, transforming our understanding of icy moon habitability.
takeaways: ESA mission to study Jupiter's three largest icy moons
Will become the first spacecraft to orbit an outer solar system moon
Focuses on Ganymede's ocean, magnetic field, and habitability

faq.question: How does JUICE differ from Europa Clipper?
faq.answer: Europa Clipper focuses exclusively on Europa with many close flybys. JUICE studies all three icy Galilean moons (Ganymede, Europa, Callisto) and ultimately orbits Ganymede.

faq.question: Why does JUICE take so long to reach Jupiter?
faq.answer: JUICE uses gravity assists from Earth, Venus, and Earth again over 8 years to build up enough velocity to reach Jupiter without requiring an enormous rocket. This fuel-efficient trajectory is necessary because JUICE carries extensive scientific instruments that add mass.
